---
title: "Arch mirror benchmark: Copenhagen"
date: "23 October 2026"
lang: en-GB
params:
  evidence_dir: "evidence"
output:
  md_document:
    variant: gfm
    preserve_yaml: true
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
evidence = params$evidence_dir
database = jsonlite::read_json(
  file.path(evidence, "database", "summary.json"), simplifyVector = TRUE
)
package = jsonlite::read_json(
  file.path(evidence, "package-confirm", "summary.json"), simplifyVector = TRUE
)
raw = read.csv(file.path(evidence, "package-confirm", "raw.csv"))
urls = c(
  Osbeck = "https://mirror.osbeck.com/archlinux/",
  dotsrc = "https://mirrors.dotsrc.org/archlinux/",
  Lysator = "https://ftp.lysator.liu.se/pub/archlinux/"
)

# Fail rather than silently dropping an unsuccessful or incomplete transfer.
stopifnot(
  all(tolower(as.character(raw$success)) == "true"),
  all(raw$phase == "package"),
  all(raw$size_download == package$package_bytes),
  length(unique(raw$sha256)) == 1L,
  unique(raw$sha256) == package$successful_sha256,
  all(is.finite(raw$time_total) & raw$time_total > 0)
)
raw$rate = raw$size_download / raw$time_total / 2^20
measurements = lapply(urls, function(url) {
  trials = raw[raw$url == url, ]
  stopifnot(
    nrow(trials) == package$rounds,
    identical(sort(trials$round), seq_len(package$rounds))
  )
  trials[order(trials$round), ]
})
stopifnot(nrow(raw) == length(urls) * package$rounds)
describe = function(trials) {
  c(
    median_rate = median(trials$rate),
    mean_rate = mean(trials$rate),
    sd_rate = sd(trials$rate),
    median_time = median(trials$time_total),
    mean_time = mean(trials$time_total)
  )
}
statistics = t(vapply(measurements, describe, numeric(5)))
osbeck = statistics["Osbeck", ]
dotsrc = statistics["dotsrc", ]
rate_advantage = 100 * (dotsrc["median_rate"] / osbeck["median_rate"] - 1)
mean_time_change = 100 * (dotsrc["mean_time"] / osbeck["mean_time"] - 1)
median_time_saved = osbeck["median_time"] - dotsrc["median_time"]
wins = sum(measurements$dotsrc$rate > measurements$Osbeck$rate)
db_rates = vapply(urls, function(url) {
  database$ranking$median_mib_per_second[database$ranking$url == url]
}, numeric(1))
format_number = function(value, digits = 2) {
  formatC(value, digits = digits, format = "f")
}
```

## Recommendation

**Osbeck first, dotsrc second, Lysator third** is the preferred general-purpose
order. Osbeck led database downloads and had lower observed mean package
completion time and variability. Your original list already started with Osbeck.
For median throughput of large packages, dotsrc is the nominal leader.

## Measurements and results

Of **`r database$screened` European HTTPS mirrors** screened,
`r database$screen_successes` passed; all `r database$finalists` finalists
passed three shuffled repeat rounds. Downloads were serial; elapsed time
included connection setup. The table uses **`r package$rounds` fresh rounds
per mirror** of one `r format_number(package$package_bytes / 2^20)` MiB Firefox
package. All `r nrow(raw)` payloads had the same SHA256.

```{r results, results='asis'}
display = data.frame(
  Mirror = names(urls),
  `Median MiB/s` = format_number(statistics[, "median_rate"]),
  `Mean ± SD MiB/s` = paste(
    format_number(statistics[, "mean_rate"]), "±",
    format_number(statistics[, "sd_rate"])
  ),
  `Mean time (s)` = format_number(statistics[, "mean_time"], 3),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(display, format = "pipe", row.names = FALSE,
             align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"))
```

MiB/s uses binary megabytes. SD is the sample standard deviation across
within-session transfers. Database median rates were **Osbeck
`r format_number(db_rates["Osbeck"])`, dotsrc
`r format_number(db_rates["dotsrc"])`, Lysator
`r format_number(db_rates["Lysator"])` MiB/s** (three rounds each).

Dotsrc's median package throughput was **`r format_number(rate_advantage, 1)`%
higher** than Osbeck's, saving `r format_number(median_time_saved, 3)` seconds
at the median. It won `r wins` of `r package$rounds` round comparisons. However,
its slower transfers made its **mean completion time
`r format_number(mean_time_change, 1)`% longer**, which supports retaining
Osbeck first when balancing speed and consistency.

## Interpretation

These descriptive results cover one host, path and day. Repeated transfers
are not independent days; no significance or confidence claims are made.
Only the database top three received the package check. Other times of day
and pacman's parallel downloads were not tested. No lasting winner or
whole-upgrade speedup is established; no system mirrorlist was changed.

Evidence: [detailed benchmark](benchmark-2026-10-23.md) and
[saved measurements](evidence/package-confirm/raw.csv).
